source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 5: Cabling
clues: the link light is on and the server can be pinged
file copies to the server crawl and often time out
the switch port counters show many late collisions and CRC errors
the server NIC was hard-set during a rebuild while the switch port was left on auto

answer.cause: a duplex mismatch between the switch port and the server NIC
answer.action: Set both ends of the link to the same speed and duplex, or set both to autonegotiate

appliesWhen: one end of a link runs full duplex and the other half duplex
explanation: A link that stays up but shows late collisions and CRC errors points to the two ends sending in different duplex modes. When one end is fixed and the other negotiates, the negotiating end often falls back to half duplex.
firstStep: Compare the speed and duplex settings on the switch port and the server NIC

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 5: Cabling
clues: the port shows no link light at all
the cable tests good and works on another PC
the NIC was manually set to 100 Mbps for an old application
the switch port is fixed at 1000 Mbps

answer.cause: a speed mismatch between the NIC and the switch port
answer.action: Set the NIC and the switch port to the same speed, or let both autonegotiate

appliesWhen: the two ends of a link are fixed at different data rates
explanation: Two ends that are fixed at different rates cannot bring the link up, so there is no link light even with a good cable. Matching the rates, or letting both ends negotiate, brings the link up.
firstStep: Check the configured speed on the NIC and on the switch port

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
clues: the PC has a link light and gets an IP address
the address is from the sales subnet, not the accounting subnet
the user moved to a new desk yesterday
other accounting PCs on the same switch reach the accounting server

answer.cause: the switch port is assigned to the wrong VLAN
answer.action: Assign the access port to the accounting VLAN

appliesWhen: an access port is a member of a different VLAN than the user's department
explanation: A port-based VLAN takes its membership from the switch port, not the PC. After a desk move, the new port can still belong to another department's VLAN, so DHCP hands out that VLAN's subnet.
firstStep: Check which VLAN the user's switch port belongs to

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
clues: hosts in VLAN 30 reach each other on the same switch
hosts in VLAN 30 on the second floor cannot reach hosts in VLAN 30 on the first floor
traffic in VLANs 10 and 20 crosses the uplink between the floors normally
the network team added VLAN 30 last week

answer.cause: VLAN 30 is not in the allowed list of the 802.1Q trunk between the switches
answer.action: Add VLAN 30 to the allowed VLANs on both ends of the trunk

appliesWhen: a VLAN works inside one switch but its tagged frames are not carried on the uplink
explanation: When a VLAN works inside each switch but not between them while other VLANs cross the uplink, the uplink is dropping that VLAN's tagged frames. Each VLAN must be permitted on the trunk at both ends.
firstStep: Check the VLANs that the uplink carries on both switches

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation
clues: frames from devices that send no tag end up in the wrong VLAN on the far switch
both switches log a warning about the link between them
tagged traffic for the other VLANs crosses the link normally
one switch was replaced and configured from an old template

answer.cause: a native VLAN mismatch on the two ends of the trunk
answer.action: Set the same native VLAN on both ends of the trunk

appliesWhen: the two ends of a trunk use different VLAN IDs for untagged frames
explanation: On an 802.1Q trunk, only the native VLAN is sent without a tag. If each end uses a different native VLAN, untagged frames leave in one VLAN and arrive in another, while tagged VLANs are not affected.
firstStep: Compare the trunk configuration on the two switches

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
clues: a port was assigned to VLAN 40 but stays inactive
the PC on that port gets no IP address
the show vlan output does not list 40 at all
ports in VLANs 10 and 20 on the same switch work

answer.cause: VLAN 40 was never created in the switch's VLAN database
answer.action: Create VLAN 40 on the switch, then confirm the port is active in it

appliesWhen: a port is assigned to a VLAN ID that the switch does not have
explanation: A switch only forwards frames for VLANs it knows. Assigning a port to a VLAN ID that the switch has no entry for leaves the port inactive.
firstStep: Run show vlan to list the VLANs that the switch knows

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
clues: hosts in the new VLAN 50 reach each other
they cannot reach servers or hosts in any other VLAN
the hosts use 10.50.0.1 as their default gateway and cannot ping it
the layer 3 switch routes between the older VLANs

answer.cause: the switch virtual interface for VLAN 50 is missing or shut down
answer.action: Create the VLAN 50 interface on the layer 3 switch with the gateway address and enable it

appliesWhen: the hosts of a VLAN have no working gateway address on the layer 3 switch
explanation: Hosts in a VLAN use the SVI's address as their default gateway for inter-VLAN routing. If that virtual interface was not created or is down, the hosts work inside the VLAN but cannot leave it.
firstStep: Check that the VLAN 50 interface exists and is up on the layer 3 switch

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
clues: the IP phones get addresses from the user data subnet
calls break up when users download large files
the PCs plugged into the back of the phones work normally
the phone system vendor asked for phone traffic to be kept apart

answer.cause: no voice VLAN is configured on the access ports
answer.action: Configure a voice VLAN on the access ports so the phones tag their traffic into it

appliesWhen: phone traffic shares the data VLAN with no separation or priority
explanation: A voice VLAN keeps phone traffic apart from PC traffic on the same port and lets it be given priority. Without it, the phones sit in the data VLAN and compete with large downloads.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
clues: the network slowed to a halt minutes after a second cable was connected between two switches
switch CPU use is near 100 percent
broadcast traffic floods every port
the MAC address tables keep changing for the same hosts

answer.cause: a switching loop because spanning tree is disabled on the switches
answer.action: Remove the extra cable, then enable Spanning Tree Protocol on all switches

appliesWhen: two switches have more than one active path between them with no loop prevention
explanation: A redundant link with no loop prevention lets broadcasts circle forever and makes the MAC tables flap. STP blocks the redundant path so that only one active path remains.
firstStep: Disconnect the cable that was just added between the switches

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture
clues: traffic between floors passes through an old access switch in a closet
the uplinks on the new core switch are in the blocking state
every switch uses the default priority
the old closet switch has the lowest MAC address on the network

answer.cause: an old access switch was elected as the spanning tree root bridge
answer.action: Lower the bridge priority on the core switch so it becomes the root bridge

appliesWhen: a weak switch with the lowest bridge ID becomes the center of the spanning tree
explanation: STP elects the bridge with the lowest bridge ID, which is the priority and then the MAC address. With default priorities, the oldest switch can win and pull traffic through a slow path.
firstStep: Check which switch is the root bridge

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture
clues: fast-booting PCs get a 169.254 address
a minute later a DHCP renew gets a correct address
the switch ports turn green only about 30 seconds after the PC links up
the switches run the original 802.1D protocol

answer.cause: access ports that pass through the spanning tree listening and learning states before they forward
answer.action: Configure the access ports as edge (PortFast) ports or move the switches to RSTP

appliesWhen: host ports wait through the 802.1D listening and learning delays before they forward
explanation: Under 802.1D a new port blocks, listens, and learns for about 30 seconds before it forwards, so a fast PC sends its DHCP request too early. Edge ports or RSTP let host ports forward at once.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
clues: small pings and logins to the storage array work
large copies to the storage array stall
the server and storage NICs were changed to 9000 bytes last night
one switch in the path still uses the default 1500 bytes

answer.cause: jumbo frames are enabled on the hosts but not on every switch in the path
answer.action: Enable the same jumbo frame MTU on every switch and NIC in the storage path

appliesWhen: the devices along one path do not all use the same frame size
explanation: Jumbo frames work only when every device in the path supports the same larger MTU. A switch left at 1500 bytes drops the large frames, so only small packets get through.
firstStep: Ping the storage array with large packets that may not be fragmented

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
clues: four uplinks were bundled into one logical link on the first switch
the bundle shows down or only one link carries traffic
the ports on the second switch are still set up as single ports
the cables all test good

answer.cause: the link aggregation group is configured on only one side
answer.action: Configure the same LACP group on the member ports of both switches

appliesWhen: several ports are bundled at one end of a link but not at the other
explanation: LACP binds several physical ports into one logical link only when both ends agree. If one side treats the ports as single links, the bundle does not form correctly.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
need: route traffic between the VLANs without buying a separate router
clues: the core switch supports layer 3 routing
each VLAN needs a default gateway address
the routing must happen inside the switch itself

answer.item: A switch virtual interface (SVI) for each VLAN

appliesWhen: a layer 3 switch must act as the default gateway for its VLANs
explanation: An SVI is a logical interface for a VLAN with an IP address. Hosts use it as their default gateway, and the layer 3 switch routes between VLANs.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
need: create the same VLANs on forty Cisco switches without configuring each one by hand
clues: all the switches are from one vendor
new VLANs are added every month
the VLAN list should be kept in one place and copied out
appliesWhen: a VLAN list must be shared from one switch to many in the same domain
explanation: VTP is a Cisco protocol that copies the VLAN database to all switches in the same domain. It removes the need to add each VLAN on every switch.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
need: keep the finance computers in their own broadcast domain even though they sit on three floors
clues: the floors share the same switches
the finance hosts must not see other departments' broadcasts
the users must not need new IP settings when they change ports on their floor

answer.item: A dedicated finance VLAN on the access ports

appliesWhen: hosts in different places must form one isolated broadcast domain
explanation: A VLAN groups hosts into one broadcast domain no matter where they connect. Finance traffic is isolated from the other departments on the same switches.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
need: carry the traffic of six VLANs over one cable between two switches
clues: the switches are from different vendors
each frame must keep its VLAN identity across the link
only one port on each switch is free

answer.item: An 802.1Q trunk port with VLAN tagging

appliesWhen: frames of many VLANs must share one link between switches
explanation: 802.1Q adds a tag to each frame that names its VLAN, so one trunk link can carry many VLANs. It is the IEEE standard, so it works between vendors.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation
need: stop untagged frames on the trunks from landing in a user VLAN
clues: the auditors flagged VLAN 1 as a security risk
no device on the trunks needs to send untagged frames
the user data is in VLANs 10 to 40

answer.item: A native VLAN set to an unused VLAN ID

appliesWhen: untagged trunk traffic should go to a dead-end VLAN
explanation: The native VLAN carries the untagged frames of a trunk and defaults to VLAN 1. Changing it to an unused VLAN sends untagged traffic nowhere.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
need: keep the IP phone traffic apart from the PC that plugs into the back of each phone
clues: the phone and the PC share one switch port
calls must get priority over file downloads
the phones support tagging their own frames

answer.item: A voice VLAN on the access ports

appliesWhen: phone and PC traffic arrive on the same access port and must be separated
explanation: A voice VLAN puts the phone's traffic in its own VLAN while the PC stays in the data VLAN on the same port. The voice traffic can then be given priority.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
need: give the file server more bandwidth to the switch and keep it online if one cable fails
clues: the server has four gigabit NICs
the switch has free ports beside the server's port
all the links must act as one logical connection
appliesWhen: several physical ports must work as one logical link for speed and redundancy
explanation: LACP bundles several physical ports into one logical link. Traffic is shared across the members, and the link stays up if one member fails.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 5: Cabling
need: connect an old controller that cannot autonegotiate to a new switch port
clues: the controller supports only 100 Mbps full duplex
the switch port links at the wrong mode on auto
the link must not drop to half duplex

answer.item: Manually set speed and duplex that match on both ends

appliesWhen: a device cannot negotiate and the port must be set to match it
explanation: When one end cannot negotiate, the other end must be set by hand to the same speed and duplex. A match on both ends avoids a mismatch and its errors.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
need: add a second cable between two switches for redundancy without causing a loop
clues: the second path must take over if the first fails
broadcast storms must not occur
the redundant path should stay idle while the first one works
appliesWhen: redundant switch links must be kept loop-free with one path blocked
explanation: STP finds redundant paths and blocks all but one, so frames cannot loop. If the active path fails, it unblocks the backup.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture
need: recover from a failed uplink in well under a second so voice calls do not drop
clues: the switches have redundant uplinks
the original 802.1D protocol takes up to a minute to recover
loops must still be prevented
appliesWhen: loop prevention must react to a failed link in milliseconds
explanation: RSTP, defined in 802.1w, detects and corrects link failures in milliseconds instead of the long delays of 802.1D. It still keeps the topology loop-free.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture
need: make the new core switch the center of the loop-free topology
clues: all switches use the default settings
an older access switch has the lowest MAC address
the choice must not depend on MAC addresses

answer.item: A lower bridge priority on the core switch

appliesWhen: a chosen switch must win the root bridge election
explanation: The root bridge is the switch with the lowest bridge ID, made of a priority and the MAC address. Setting a lower priority on the core switch makes it win.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 3: Network Addressing, Routing, and Switching
need: cut the overhead of large transfers between the virtual hosts and the storage network
clues: every switch and NIC in the storage path supports it
the traffic is mostly large block transfers
the standard 1500-byte frames create too many headers

answer.item: Jumbo frames with an MTU of about 9000 bytes

appliesWhen: large transfers on a path where every device supports bigger frames
explanation: Jumbo frames carry more than 1500 bytes of payload, so fewer frames and headers are needed for the same data. Every device in the path must support them.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: the APs in two offices next door are set to 3 and 5 on the 2.4 GHz band
throughput drops when both offices are busy
a Wi-Fi analyzer shows the two signals on top of each other
signal strength is good

answer.cause: the two APs use overlapping 2.4 GHz channels
answer.action: Move the APs to non-overlapping channels such as 1 and 6

appliesWhen: nearby APs share overlapping parts of the 2.4 GHz band
explanation: In the 2.4 GHz band, channels are 5 MHz apart and each signal is about 20 MHz wide, so only 1, 6, and 11 do not overlap. Two APs on nearby channels interfere with each other.
firstStep: Check the channels of nearby APs with a Wi-Fi analyzer

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
clues: the 2.4 GHz radio was set to 40 MHz to get more speed
clients disconnect often since the change
several neighboring networks use the same band
the 5 GHz clients are not affected

answer.cause: a bonded 40 MHz channel in the crowded 2.4 GHz band
answer.action: Set the 2.4 GHz radio back to a 20 MHz channel width

appliesWhen: a wide bonded channel is used where the band is too crowded for it
explanation: A 40 MHz channel uses most of the small 2.4 GHz band, so it overlaps every neighbor. A narrower 20 MHz channel on 1, 6, or 11 reduces the interference.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: the office is near an airport
5 GHz clients lose the network for about a minute a few times a day
the AP log shows it changed channels at those times
clients on 2.4 GHz are not affected

answer.cause: 802.11h radar detection moving the AP off its 5 GHz channel
answer.action: Set the AP to 5 GHz channels that do not require radar detection

appliesWhen: an AP must leave a 5 GHz channel each time it detects radar
explanation: 802.11h requires DFS on many 5 GHz channels: when the AP detects radar, it must leave the channel. Each move disconnects the clients for a short time.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
clues: the new security cameras do not list the network name at all
laptops and phones connect without trouble
the cameras' datasheet lists 802.11b/g/n support only
the AP was recently set up to reduce interference

answer.cause: the SSID is offered only on the 5 GHz band, which the cameras do not support
answer.action: Turn on the 2.4 GHz radio for the SSID

appliesWhen: a device supports only one band and the AP does not offer that band
explanation: Some devices, such as cameras and IoT sensors, work only in the 2.4 GHz band. If the AP broadcasts the network only at 5 GHz, those devices cannot see it.
firstStep: Check which bands the cameras support and which bands the AP broadcasts

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
clues: most dual-band laptops near the AP connect at low data rates
the 2.4 GHz radio shows 60 clients and the 5 GHz radio shows 5
the laptops join whichever band has the strongest signal
the APs are close to the users

answer.cause: dual-band clients staying on the crowded 2.4 GHz band
answer.action: Enable band steering on the APs

appliesWhen: dual-band clients pick the slower band because its signal is stronger
explanation: A client picks the band with the strongest signal, which is often 2.4 GHz even when 5 GHz would be faster. Band steering directs capable clients to 5 GHz.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: new tri-band APs were installed
a new SSID was set up for the newest band only
the latest laptops see and join the new SSID
laptops bought three years ago do not list it

answer.cause: the older laptops' Wi-Fi adapters do not support Wi-Fi 6E
answer.action: Offer the SSID on 5 GHz as well, or upgrade the older adapters

appliesWhen: the clients' adapters do not support the band that the SSID uses
explanation: Only Wi-Fi 6E adapters can use the 6 GHz band. An SSID offered only there is invisible to older laptops.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: the laptop worked at the old office
the user moved to a new office last week
other laptops in the new office connect normally
the laptop keeps trying to join a saved network that is not there

answer.cause: the laptop is still set to the network name of the old office
answer.action: Connect the laptop to the SSID of the new office

appliesWhen: a client is configured for a network name that the local APs do not broadcast
explanation: A client can talk only to APs with the same SSID. A laptop moved between sites keeps trying the old name until it is set to the local one.
firstStep: Check which network name the laptop is trying to join

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
clues: users lose the connection each time they walk to the other wing
they must pick a network again and enter a password
the APs in the new wing were set up by a contractor
the APs are managed one at a time

answer.cause: the APs in the new wing use a different SSID or passphrase from the rest
answer.action: Configure every AP with the same SSID and security settings

appliesWhen: the APs of one network do not share the same name and security settings
explanation: Clients roam between APs only when every AP offers the same ESSID with the same security. A wing of APs with different settings looks like another network.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
clues: the AP was upgraded to WPA3-only mode last night
an older label printer now fails to join
the printer sees the network name
new laptops connect normally

answer.cause: the printer does not support the encryption that the AP now requires
answer.action: Use WPA2/WPA3 transition mode, or put the printer on a separate WPA2 SSID

appliesWhen: a client cannot use the encryption protocol that the AP requires
explanation: The client and the AP must use the same encryption. An older device that supports only WPA2 cannot join a network set to WPA3 only.
firstStep: Check which security protocols the printer supports

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: unknown devices keep appearing on the wireless network
the same passphrase has been used for three years
several staff left the company this year
there is no way to tell which person a device belongs to

answer.cause: one shared passphrase that former staff still know
answer.action: Move to WPA2- or WPA3-Enterprise with 802.1X and a login for each user

appliesWhen: every user shares one key, so access cannot be removed for one person
explanation: With a pre-shared key, everyone who ever had the key can still join, and no device can be traced to a user. Enterprise authentication checks each user against a server, so leavers can be blocked.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: no user can log on to the staff wireless network since this morning
the guest network still works
the authentication server was moved to a new IP address last night
the AP log shows timeouts for each logon

answer.cause: the APs cannot reach the RADIUS server at its new address
answer.action: Update the RADIUS server address and shared secret on the controller or APs

appliesWhen: the authentication server for 802.1X logons cannot be reached
explanation: WPA2- and WPA3-Enterprise pass each logon to a central authentication server. If the APs still point to the old address, every logon times out while PSK networks keep working.
firstStep: Check the RADIUS server address configured on the APs

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: a visitor on the guest network could browse the internal file shares
guest devices get addresses from the staff subnet
the guest network name was added to the AP last week
staff and guests share the same switch uplink

answer.cause: the guest SSID is mapped to the internal staff VLAN
answer.action: Map the guest SSID to an isolated VLAN that allows internet access only

appliesWhen: guest wireless traffic lands on the internal network
explanation: A guest network must be kept apart from the main network so visitors get only internet access. Guests with staff addresses show that the guest SSID is bridged into the internal VLAN.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
clues: guests connect to the guest network and get an IP address
the terms page never appears in the browser
the guests' browsers open an HTTPS home page first
browsing to a plain HTTP site makes the page appear

answer.cause: the browser's HTTPS request cannot be redirected to the captive portal page
answer.action: Open a non-secure HTTP page to trigger the portal, and check that DNS and the firewall allow the portal

appliesWhen: the splash page that guests must accept does not load in the browser
explanation: A captive portal works by redirecting the first web request. A secure HTTPS page often refuses the redirect, so the portal never loads until the guest opens a plain HTTP page.
firstStep: Browse to a non-secure HTTP site from the guest device

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: the link between the two buildings is weak and drops often
the antennas on both roofs are vertical poles
people in nearby buildings can see the network
the buildings have clear line of sight

answer.cause: omnidirectional antennas on a building-to-building link
answer.action: Replace them with directional antennas aimed at each other

appliesWhen: a long link between two fixed points spreads its signal in every direction
explanation: An omnidirectional antenna spreads its power in all directions, so little of it reaches a distant fixed point. A directional antenna focuses the signal for a stronger, longer link.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: the signal is strong in front of the AP
it is weak beside and behind the AP
the AP is in the middle of the open floor
the installer used an antenna kit from a previous project

answer.cause: a directional antenna on an AP that must cover all around it
answer.action: Use an omnidirectional antenna on the central AP

appliesWhen: an AP in the middle of an area focuses its signal in one direction
explanation: A directional antenna focuses its power one way, so the areas to the sides and back get little signal. An omnidirectional antenna covers 360 degrees from the center.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
clues: the link was rebuilt after a storm
both antennas are aimed at each other
one antenna is now mounted on its side
the received signal is much weaker than before

answer.cause: the two antennas have different polarization
answer.action: Mount both antennas with the same polarization

appliesWhen: the sending and receiving antennas radiate along different axes
explanation: Polarization is the axis along which an antenna radiates, vertical or horizontal. Both ends of a link must use the same polarization, or much of the signal is lost.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: devices near the unit in the garage are very slow
the unit's app shows a weak link to the next unit
there is no Ethernet cable to the garage
the other units in the house work well

answer.cause: the mesh unit in the garage is too far from the other units
answer.action: Move the mesh unit closer to the next unit or add a unit between them

appliesWhen: a mesh relay has a weak wireless link to its neighbors
explanation: In a mesh network, each unit relays data over a wireless link to its neighbors. A unit placed too far away has a weak link, so every device behind it is slow.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: the 40 APs are each configured through their own web page
some APs still use last year's passphrase
channel and power settings differ from AP to AP
updates take two days to apply

answer.cause: standalone APs set up one at a time with different settings
answer.action: Move to lightweight APs managed from a wireless LAN controller

appliesWhen: many APs are each managed on their own without central control
explanation: Autonomous APs are configured one by one, so in a large network their settings drift apart. Lightweight APs take their settings from one controller.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
clues: after a firewall change, the branch APs stopped broadcasting
the APs power on and get IP addresses
the APs' status lights show they are searching
the APs are managed from the head office

answer.cause: the lightweight APs cannot reach their wireless LAN controller
answer.action: Allow the traffic between the APs and the controller through the firewall

appliesWhen: managed APs lose the path to the device that holds their settings
explanation: Lightweight APs take their configuration from a wireless LAN controller. If a firewall blocks the controller, the APs boot but never get the settings to broadcast.
firstStep: Check that the APs can reach the controller's address

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: choose channels for three APs in the 2.4 GHz band
clues: the APs' coverage areas overlap
the APs must not interfere with each other
each AP uses a 20 MHz channel
appliesWhen: nearby 2.4 GHz APs must not overlap
explanation: In the 2.4 GHz band, only channels 1, 6, and 11 do not overlap. Giving each AP one of them avoids interference.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: get the highest throughput for a few video editing stations
clues: the stations are close to the AP
the 5 GHz band in the building is almost empty
the AP and stations support Wi-Fi 6

answer.item: An 80 MHz or 160 MHz channel width on 5 GHz

appliesWhen: a quiet band has room for bonded channels
explanation: Channel bonding joins channels into a wider one, which carries more data. In a quiet 5 GHz band there is room for 80 or 160 MHz channels without much interference.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: use the 5 GHz band in a country whose regulator protects radar systems
clues: the APs must avoid channels used by radar
they must lower transmit power where required
the network must operate legally
appliesWhen: regulators require radar avoidance and power control on 5 GHz
explanation: 802.11h adds Dynamic Frequency Selection, which moves off channels where radar is found, and Transmit Power Control. It meets regulatory rules for the 5 GHz band.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
need: cover a large warehouse with tall metal shelves for older handheld scanners
clues: the scanners support only 802.11b/g/n
range matters more than speed
the signal must pass through many obstacles
appliesWhen: range and support for older clients matter more than throughput
explanation: The longer waves of 2.4 GHz travel farther and pass obstacles better than 5 or 6 GHz. Older 802.11b/g devices work only there.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: give a crowded open-plan office faster Wi-Fi with less interference
clues: neighboring offices fill the lower band
most laptops are from the last six years
the APs are mounted close to the users
appliesWhen: clients need more speed and channels than 2.4 GHz gives and support the band
explanation: 5 GHz offers many more non-overlapping channels and higher speeds than 2.4 GHz, with less interference. Its shorter range suits APs placed close to users.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: give new Wi-Fi 6E laptops uncongested spectrum with many wide channels
clues: both lower bands are crowded
all the target laptops are new
the APs are tri-band
appliesWhen: every client supports the newest, least crowded band
explanation: Wi-Fi 6E adds the 6 GHz band, which gives more channels and bandwidth and less interference. Only 6E clients can use it.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
need: move dual-band clients off the busy lower band automatically
clues: the same network name is on both bands
clients join the band with the strongest signal
most clients can use both bands
appliesWhen: dual-band clients must be directed to the better band
explanation: Band steering makes the AP answer capable clients on 5 GHz, so they do not stay on 2.4 GHz only because its signal is stronger.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: let users walk through the whole building without joining a new network
clues: the building has 25 APs
users must see one network name
the APs connect to the same subnet

answer.item: One ESSID shared by all the APs

appliesWhen: many APs must appear as one wireless network
explanation: An ESSID is the network name shared by all APs in an extended service set. Clients roam between APs with the same name and security.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: find out which AP a problem laptop is connected to in a survey log
clues: all the APs use the same network name
the log lists each radio's hardware address
the result must point to one AP
appliesWhen: one AP radio must be told apart from others with the same network name
explanation: The BSSID is the MAC address of an AP radio, so it is unique for each AP. The ESSID is shared and cannot show which AP the client uses.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: cover a large site where cables cannot be run to each AP
clues: the network must keep working if one unit fails
units must relay traffic for each other
only one unit has a wired connection
appliesWhen: wireless units must relay data for each other and heal around failures
explanation: In a mesh network, each node relays data to the others and traffic reroutes when a node fails. Only one node needs a wired link.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: share files between two laptops at a field site that has no access point
clues: no network equipment is on site
the setup is temporary
the laptops are in the same room
appliesWhen: devices must connect directly with no AP
explanation: An ad hoc network lets devices connect directly to each other with no central AP. It suits short, temporary setups.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: link the main building to a warehouse 500 meters away without digging a trench
clues: the roofs have clear line of sight
only the two sites need to be connected
the link must carry the warehouse's whole LAN traffic

answer.item: A point-to-point wireless link with directional antennas

appliesWhen: two fixed sites need one dedicated wireless link
explanation: A point-to-point link joins exactly two endpoints, often between buildings. Directional antennas focus the signal for the distance.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: connect the office laptops to the wired LAN and the internet
clues: the laptops must reach the file servers
access must be managed centrally
ceiling-mounted APs are wired to the switches
appliesWhen: clients reach the wired network through central APs
explanation: In an infrastructure network, clients connect through APs that bridge them to the wired LAN. It is the usual type for offices.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: secure a small office network with one passphrase that resists offline guessing
clues: there is no authentication server
all the devices are new
the staff choose simple passwords
appliesWhen: a passphrase network must resist offline dictionary attacks
explanation: WPA3-Personal replaces the PSK exchange with Simultaneous Authentication of Equals. SAE resists offline dictionary attacks and gives forward secrecy even with simple passwords.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: secure a network whose devices support WPA2 but not WPA3
clues: the handheld devices cannot be upgraded
the policy bans WEP and TKIP
the strongest option the devices offer must be used
appliesWhen: the clients support WPA2 at most
explanation: WPA2 requires CCMP, which uses 128-bit AES. It is the strongest choice when devices cannot use WPA3.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: give each employee their own wireless login and block it when they leave
clues: the company has a directory of user accounts
a RADIUS server is available
a shared passphrase is not allowed
appliesWhen: each user must log on with their own credentials checked by a server
explanation: Enterprise mode sends each logon to an authentication server through 802.1X. Each user has their own credentials, so one account can be disabled without changing anyone else's.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: give visitors internet access without letting them reach internal servers
clues: visitors bring their own devices
staff data must stay protected
visitor traffic should be limited in bandwidth

answer.item: A separate guest SSID on an isolated network

appliesWhen: visitors need internet access but no access to the main network
explanation: A guest network is a separate SSID that gives internet access while keeping visitors apart from the main network. Bandwidth limits can protect staff traffic.

source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 6: Wireless Networking
need: make hotel-style guests accept the acceptable use policy before they browse
clues: guests use the visitor network
each guest must see the terms first
no user accounts are created for guests
appliesWhen: guests must see and accept a web page before they get access
explanation: A captive portal redirects a new guest's browser to a page with the terms or a login. Access opens only after the guest accepts.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: cover an open-plan floor evenly from one AP in the center
clues: users sit all around the AP
the floor has few walls
no area needs extra range
appliesWhen: the signal must reach all directions around the AP
explanation: An omnidirectional antenna sends the signal 360 degrees around it. It suits an AP in the middle of an open area.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: send a strong signal down a long, narrow corridor from an AP at one end
clues: the coverage area is in one direction only
the signal must reach far
nearby rooms should not get the signal
appliesWhen: the signal must be focused in one direction for distance
explanation: A directional antenna focuses power in one direction, which gives a stronger signal over a longer distance. It does not waste signal where it is not needed.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: manage 200 APs across a campus from one place with smooth roaming
clues: firmware and settings must be pushed to all APs at once
radio settings should be tuned centrally
the network will keep growing

answer.item: Lightweight APs with a wireless LAN controller

appliesWhen: a large network needs central management of its APs
explanation: Lightweight APs hand configuration, firmware, RF tuning, and roaming to a wireless LAN controller. One controller manages every AP, so it scales well.

source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions
need: add one AP to a small shop that has no other network equipment to manage it
clues: there is no controller
the AP will be configured through its own web page
only one AP is needed
appliesWhen: a small site has one standalone AP with no controller
explanation: An autonomous AP works on its own and is configured directly. It suits small sites where a controller is not needed.
